audit_objective: Determine historical AIS information for MV Wakashio publicly recoverable from legitimate investigation and public sources

sources.source_name: Japan Transport Safety Board (JTSB) Marine Accident Investigation Report
sources.authoritative_body: Japan Transport Safety Board (Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism - MLIT)
sources.document_type: Official Marine Accident Safety Investigation Report (PDF)
sources.classification_label: AIS-derived graphical evidence only (with sparse narrative milestones - Tier C)

evaluation.timestamps: Selective discrete milestone timestamps in narrative and nautical chart figures (e.g. 2020-07-25 14:00, 18:00, 19:00, 19:15, 19:25 local / 10:00 to 15:25 UTC)
evaluation.latitude_longitude: Discrete milestone coordinates in text (e.g., initial approach point, course change waypoint, and reef impact position: 20°26.4' S, 057°44.4' E)
evaluation.sog: Selective cruise speed mentions (~11.0 to 11.5 knots prior to impact; 0 knots post-grounding)
evaluation.cog: Selective course mentions (~240° to 243° on approach track)
evaluation.navigation_status: Contextual operational status in narrative ('Under way using engine' transition to 'Aground')
evaluation.exact_temporal_resolution: Sparse narrative milestones (intervals ranging from 15 minutes to several hours; approximately 6 discrete points)
evaluation.exact_spatial_coverage: East of Mauritius (approach vector ~100 nm out to reef impact at Pointe d'Esny)
evaluation.legally_legitimately_extractable: Report is public domain government safety material, but data exists strictly as narrative text and vector-rendered chart graphics in a PDF; no digital CSV/NMEA stream is published or attached

sources.assessment: High historical ground-truth value for verifying incident coordinates and timeline, but completely unusable for operational candidate generation. Lacks multi-vessel background traffic and lacks continuous dynamic time series.

sources.source_name: Mauritius Court of Investigation Report on the Grounding of MV Wakashio
sources.authoritative_body: Court of Investigation, Republic of Mauritius (Former Judge Asraf Caunhye presiding)
sources.url: Official Government of Mauritius Publication / Judicial Repository
sources.classification_label: AIS-derived graphical evidence only (with sparse narrative milestones - Tier C)

evaluation.timestamps: Milestone timestamps derived from National Coast Guard (NCG) radar tracking and ship Voyage Data Recorder (VDR) (e.g. 18:00 radar contact, 19:10, 19:25 grounding, 20:07 NCG VHF attempt)
evaluation.latitude_longitude: Reef impact location (20°26'24" S, 057°44'24" E / -20.4400°, 57.7400°) and distance-to-shore narrative marks (e.g., 1.5 nm off coast)
evaluation.sog: Narrative mentions of steady approach speed (~11 knots)
evaluation.navigation_status: Narrative legal descriptions ('steaming towards coast', 'stranded on reef')
evaluation.vessel_scope: Wakashio only (single vessel; local NCG craft mentioned days later during response)
evaluation.exact_spatial_coverage: Mauritius territorial sea and coastal radar arc off Pointe d'Esny
evaluation.legally_legitimately_extractable: Public judicial document, but contains no structured tabular digital trajectory dataset

sources.assessment: Provides authoritative legal confirmation of vessel identity, timeline, and watchkeeping failure, but zero digital multi-vessel trajectory data.

sources.source_name: Panama Maritime Authority (AMP) Safety Investigation Documentation
sources.authoritative_body: Panama Maritime Authority (Directorate General of Merchant Marine - DIAM)
sources.reference_code: AMP Casualty Investigation File / Safety Notices 2020-2023
sources.document_type: Flag State Preliminary and Final Casualty Reports / Marine Notices
sources.url: https://panamamaritimeauthority.com / AMP Department of Maritime Investigation
sources.classification_label: AIS-derived graphical evidence only (referencing commercial datasets - Tier E)

evaluation.timestamps: Voyage-level departure/transit milestones (Singapore departure 2020-07-14 to grounding 2020-07-25 19:25 local)
evaluation.latitude_longitude: Final grounding location and small-scale voyage overview route markers
evaluation.cog: Waypoints of planned route vs altered route
evaluation.exact_spatial_coverage: Trans-Indian Ocean transit (Malacca Strait to Mauritius)
evaluation.legally_legitimately_extractable: Summary reports are public; underlying satellite AIS data acquired from commercial providers (Pole Star / exactEarth) remains confidential state casualty files

sources.assessment: Confirms flag state verification of voyage track and cause (diversion to search for cell signal), but provides no open digital AIS records.

sources.source_name: Authoritative Multilateral & Technical Investigation Records (IMO, Cedre, ITOPF)
sources.authoritative_body: International Maritime Organization (GISIS), Cedre France, and ITOPF
sources.reference_code: IMO GISIS Marine Casualty Record; Cedre Technical Information Bulletin; ITOPF Country Profile
sources.document_type: Multilateral Casualty Records and Environmental Response Bulletins
sources.classification_label: Not actually AIS (IMO GISIS contains single casualty point - Tier C)

evaluation.latitude_longitude: Single point casualty coordinate: 20°26'00" S, 057°44'00" E
evaluation.exact_spatial_coverage: Point location at Pointe d'Esny reef
evaluation.legally_legitimately_extractable: Summary records viewable by registered maritime stakeholders; no dynamic AIS time series exists

sources.assessment: Official institutional record confirming casualty metadata; completely lacks trajectory data or surrounding traffic.

sources.source_name: Peer-Reviewed Academic and Scientific Literature on Wakashio Tracking
sources.authoritative_body: Various Academic Journals (Remote Sensing, Marine Pollution Bulletin, Current Science, etc.)
sources.reference_code: e.g., Remote Sensing 2020/2021; Indian Academy of Sciences 2021; Journal of Operational Oceanography 2021
sources.classification_label: AIS-derived graphical evidence only (referencing proprietary datasets - Tier E)

evaluation.timestamps: Plotted as axis tick labels on track maps and velocity graphs
evaluation.latitude_longitude: Plotted cartographically on GIS figures and satellite overlay images
evaluation.sog: Plotted as time-series curve figures (showing ~11 knots plunging to 0 knots at grounding)
evaluation.vessel_scope: Wakashio only (occasionally regional traffic density rasters without vessel identifiers)
evaluation.exact_temporal_resolution: Derived from ~1-5 minute satellite AIS, but published only as rendered static raster/vector graphics
evaluation.exact_spatial_coverage: Southern Indian Ocean and Mauritius EEZ
evaluation.legally_legitimately_extractable: Raw AIS trajectories are omitted from supplementary data files due to commercial End User License Agreements (EULAs) with vendors like MarineTraffic, Spire, or exactEarth which strictly forbid redistributing raw AIS records

sources.assessment: Researchers utilized proprietary commercial AIS data for visualization and drift verification, but licensing restrictions preclude publishing machine-readable multi-vessel datasets.

sources.source_name: Commercial Maritime Analytics Investigative Releases (Windward, Lloyd's List, Forbes)
sources.authoritative_body: Windward Ltd., Lloyd's List Intelligence, Forbes (Investigative reporting by N. Degnarain)
sources.reference_code: Windward Maritime Risk Analysis (Aug 2020); Forbes Investigative Series (Aug-Oct 2020)
sources.document_type: Web Investigative Articles, Platform Screenshots, and Interactive Maps
sources.classification_label: AIS-derived graphical evidence only (referencing commercial platform data - Tier E)

evaluation.timestamps: Exposed selectively in callouts, infographics, and article narrative
evaluation.latitude_longitude: Depicted graphically on interactive GIS maps and static screenshot graphics
evaluation.sog: Exposed in infographic charts (~11 knots constant speed)
evaluation.cog: Depicted as straight trackline showing 1,200-mile approach without course alteration
evaluation.vessel_scope: Wakashio highlighted; background shipping lanes shown as aggregated density heatmaps without individual vessel tracks
evaluation.exact_temporal_resolution: Continuous proprietary telemetry (downsampled to infographic milestones in publications)
evaluation.exact_spatial_coverage: Trans-Indian Ocean track approaching Mauritius coast
evaluation.legally_legitimately_extractable: Proprietary commercial intelligence; no open tabular CSV/JSON download exists

sources.assessment: Provides vivid, compelling graphical and analytical evidence disproving adverse weather maneuvers, but provides zero open-access machine-readable trajectory data.

operational_pipeline_evaluation.reason: Blind candidate generation requires open, spatio-temporally bounded multi-vessel trajectories across the Mauritius EEZ during July 25 to August 11, 2020. Public investigation sources provide only sparse single-vessel milestone coordinates for MV Wakashio itself.
operational_pipeline_evaluation.scientific_integrity_guardrail: Extracting single-vessel Wakashio coordinates from investigation reports and feeding them into the candidate generator would introduce artificial 1-candidate cheat bias with 100% false certainty, completely invalidating the blind validation protocol.
operational_pipeline_evaluation.synthetic_interpolation_guardrail: Synthesizing or interpolating high-frequency AIS pings from sparse milestone coordinates or digitized map graphics violates project scientific constraints ('Do NOT scrape images/maps and convert them into fake AIS points; Do NOT interpolate sparse public observations').
